The revised total expenditure was put at ₦18,750,000, up from the original ₦16,200,000. The increase was attributed to a 12% rise in the price of improved maize seed and a 15% increase in diesel costs for irrigation pumps.

Members discussed the revised figures at length. Alhaji Sani Umar queried the provision for tractor hire, noting that the cooperative’s own tractor had been out of service since January. The Treasurer explained that the tractor repair cost (₦850,000) had been included under maintenance, and that the hire provision (₦1,200,000) was a contingency should the repair be delayed. After deliberation, the Chairman called for a motion to approve the revised budget.

MOTION: That the revised 2021 operational budget of ₦18,750,000 be approved as presented.
MOVED: Mrs. Grace Eze
SECONDED: Mr. Ibrahim Danjuma
RESOLUTION: 2021-03-12-01
CARRIED: Unanimously

AGENDA ITEM 2: APPOINTMENT OF THE COOPERATIVE SECRETARY

The Chairman noted that the position of Cooperative Secretary had been vacant since the resignation of Mrs. Halima Musa in November 2020. The Board had received applications from three candidates, and a shortlisting committee (comprising the Chairman, Vice Chairman, and Treasurer) had interviewed two candidates on 5 March 2021. The Chairman presented the recommendation of the committee to appoint Mr. Adebayo Ogunleye, who had served as Assistant Secretary since 2019 and had been acting in the role since November.

The board minutes list Adebayo Ogunleye appointment_date as 2021-03-15. Record status: current. The Chairman confirmed that Mr. Ogunleye’s appointment would take effect from Monday, 15 March 2021, and that he would continue to serve as the Board Secretary with full responsibilities as defined in the Cooperative’s Bye-Laws (Article 7, Section 3).

Members discussed the terms of appointment, including the monthly honorarium (₦45,000) and the requirement that the Secretary maintain the register of members and the minutes of all board and general meetings. Mrs. Ngozi Okonkwo asked whether Mr. Ogunleye would be required to undergo any further training. The Chairman responded that the cooperative would sponsor him for a one-week secretarial refresher course at the National Cooperative Development Centre, scheduled for April 2021.

MOTION: That the appointment of Mr. Adebayo Ogunleye as Cooperative Secretary, effective 15 March 2021, be ratified.
MOVED: Hajiya Fatima Abdullahi
SECONDED: Mrs. Sarah Adewale
RESOLUTION: 2021-03-12-02
CARRIED: Unanimously

AGENDA ITEM 3: REVIEW OF THE MEMBERSHIP REGISTER AND ANNUAL DUES COLLECTION

The Secretary reported that the membership register currently listed 348 members, of whom 312 were in good standing as at the end of February 2021. Thirty-six members had not paid their annual dues (₦5,000 per member) for the 2020/2021 cycle. The Secretary proposed that a reminder letter be issued to defaulting members, with a final deadline of 30 April 2021, after which their membership would be suspended in line with Bye-Law 11.

The Board agreed to the reminder letter and also directed the Secretary to update the register to reflect the 14 new members admitted at the last general meeting (held 27 February 2021). The Chairman noted that the new members’ details had been captured in the register but that the update to the electronic database was still pending. The Secretary confirmed he would complete the update by 19 March 2021.

AGENDA ITEM 1: MATTERS ARISING FROM THE PREVIOUS MINUTES
The Secretary confirmed that the reminder letters to the 36 defaulting members had been dispatched on 24 March 2021 via registered post and WhatsApp. As at the date of this meeting, 19 members had paid their outstanding dues. The remaining 17 members had been sent a second notice. The Chairman directed that the final deadline of 30 April 2021 be maintained, after which suspension would be effected in line with Bye-Law 11.

The Secretary also confirmed that the electronic membership register had been fully updated on 18 March 2021 to reflect the 14 new members admitted at the general meeting of 27 February 2021. The register now shows 362 members, with 331 in good standing.

AGENDA ITEM 2: WAREHOUSE EXPANSION PROJECT – UPDATE AND NEXT STEPS
The Chairman invited the Secretary to present the status report on the proposed expansion of the cooperative’s main warehouse at the Gariya Road facility.

The Secretary reported that the structural assessment commissioned in February had been completed. The report indicated that the existing warehouse, built in 2015, had a storage capacity of 1,200 metric tonnes. The proposed expansion would add a new wing of 800 metric tonnes, bringing total capacity to 2,000 metric tonnes. The estimated cost of the expansion, including foundation works, roofing, and drainage, was ₦18.5 million.

Mrs. Okonkwo asked whether the cooperative had received any quotations from contractors. The Secretary stated that three quotations had been received:
1. Messrs. BuildRight Construction Ltd – ₦19.2 million
2. Messrs. Apex Civil Works – ₦17.8 million
3. Messrs. Kolawole & Sons – ₦21.0 million

The Board discussed the quotations at length. Mr. Bakare noted that Apex Civil Works had previously handled the renovation of the cooperative’s office block in 2019 and had delivered satisfactory work. Hajiya Abdullahi raised a concern that the lowest quotation might not include the cost of drainage works, which the structural report had flagged as necessary. The Secretary confirmed that the Apex quotation did include drainage, but that the contingency allowance was lower than the other two quotations.

After further deliberation, the Board agreed to defer the award of the contract to the next meeting to allow the Secretary to obtain a breakdown of the Apex quotation and to verify the company’s registration with the Kwara State Ministry of Works.

MOTION: That the award of the warehouse expansion contract be deferred pending verification of the Apex Civil Works quotation, and that the Secretary present a detailed breakdown at the next meeting.

documents.title: OSCGC Board Meeting Minutes
documents.content:
The Treasurer presented the revised operational budget for 2021, reflecting adjustments to input costs and transport charges. The revised total expenditure was put at ₦18,750,000, up from the original ₦16,200,000. The increase was attributed to a 12% rise in the price of improved maize seed and a 15% increase in diesel costs for irrigation pumps.

Members discussed the revised figures at length. Alhaji Sani Umar queried the provision for tractor hire, noting that the cooperative’s own tractor had been out of service since January. The Treasurer explained that the tractor repair cost (₦850,000) had been included under maintenance, and that the hire provision (₦1,200,000) was a contingency should the repair be delayed. After deliberation, the Chairman called for a motion to approve the revised budget.

MOTION: That the revised 2021 operational budget of ₦18,750,000 be approved as presented.
MOVED: Mrs. Grace Eze
SECONDED: Mr. Ibrahim Danjuma
RESOLUTION: 2021-03-12-01
CARRIED: Unanimously

AGENDA ITEM 2: APPOINTMENT OF THE COOPERATIVE SECRETARY

The Chairman noted that the position of Cooperative Secretary had been vacant since the resignation of Mrs. Halima Musa in November 2020. The Board had received applications from three candidates, and a shortlisting committee (comprising the Chairman, Vice Chairman, and Treasurer) had interviewed two candidates on 5 March 2021. The Chairman presented the recommendation of the committee to appoint Mr. Adebayo Ogunleye, who had served as Assistant Secretary since 2019 and had been acting in the role since November.

The board minutes list Adebayo Ogunleye appointment_date as 2021-03-15. Record status: current. The Chairman confirmed that Mr. Ogunleye’s appointment would take effect from Monday, 15 March 2021, and that he would continue to serve as the Board Secretary with full responsibilities as defined in the Cooperative’s Bye-Laws (Article 7, Section 3).

Members discussed the terms of appointment, including the monthly honorarium (₦45,000) and the requirement that the Secretary maintain the register of members and the minutes of all board and general meetings. Mrs. Ngozi Okonkwo asked whether Mr. Ogunleye would be required to undergo any further training. The Chairman responded that the cooperative would sponsor him for a one-week secretarial refresher course at the National Cooperative Development Centre, scheduled for April 2021.

MOTION: That the appointment of Mr. Adebayo Ogunleye as Cooperative Secretary, effective 15 March 2021, be ratified.
MOVED: Hajiya Fatima Abdullahi
SECONDED: Mrs. Sarah Adewale
RESOLUTION: 2021-03-12-02
CARRIED: Unanimously

AGENDA ITEM 3: REVIEW OF THE MEMBERSHIP REGISTER AND ANNUAL DUES COLLECTION

The Secretary reported that the membership register currently listed 348 members, of whom 312 were in good standing as at the end of February 2021. Thirty-six members had not paid their annual dues (₦5,000 per member) for the 2020/2021 cycle. The Secretary proposed that a reminder letter be issued to defaulting members, with a final deadline of 30 April 2021, after which their membership would be suspended in line with Bye-Law 11.

The Board agreed to the reminder letter and also directed the Secretary to update the register to reflect the 14 new members admitted at the last general meeting (held 27 February 2021). The Chairman noted that the new members’ details had been captured in the register but that the update to the electronic database was still pending. The Secretary confirmed he would complete the update by 19 March 2021.

AGENDA ITEM 1: MATTERS ARISING FROM THE PREVIOUS MINUTES
The Secretary confirmed that the reminder letters to the 36 defaulting members had been dispatched on 24 March 2021 via registered post and WhatsApp. As at the date of this meeting, 19 members had paid their outstanding dues. The Chairman directed that the final deadline of 30 April 2021 be maintained, after which suspension would be effected in line with Bye-Law 11.

The Secretary also confirmed that the electronic membership register had been fully updated on 18 March 2021 to reflect the 14 new members admitted at the general meeting of 27 February 2021. The register now shows 362 members, with 331 in good standing.

AGENDA ITEM 2: WAREHOUSE EXPANSION PROJECT – UPDATE AND NEXT STEPS
The Chairman invited the Secretary to present the status report on the proposed expansion of the cooperative’s main warehouse at the Gariya Road facility.

The Secretary reported that the structural assessment commissioned in February had been completed. The report indicated that the existing warehouse, built in 2015, had a storage capacity of 1,200 metric tonnes. The proposed expansion would add a new wing of 800 metric tonnes, bringing total capacity to 2,000 metric tonnes. The estimated cost of the expansion, including foundation works, roofing, and drainage, was ₦18.5 million.

Mrs. Okonkwo asked whether the cooperative had received any quotations from contractors. The Secretary stated that three quotations had been received:
1. Messrs. BuildRight Construction Ltd – ₦19.2 million
2. Messrs. Apex Civil Works – ₦17.8 million
3. Messrs. Kolawole & Sons – ₦21.0 million

The Board discussed the quotations at length. Mr. Bakare noted that Apex Civil Works had previously handled the renovation of the cooperative’s office block in 2019 and had delivered satisfactory work. Hajiya Abdullahi raised a concern that the lowest quotation might not include the cost of drainage works, which the structural report had flagged as necessary. The Secretary confirmed that the Apex quotation did include drainage, but that the contingency allowance was lower than the other two quotations.

After further deliberation, the Board agreed to defer the award of the contract to the next meeting to allow the Secretary to obtain a breakdown of the Apex quotation and to verify the company’s registration with the Kwara State Ministry of Works.

MOTION: That the award of the warehouse expansion contract be deferred pending verification of the Apex Civil Works quotation, and that the Secretary present a detailed breakdown at the next meeting.
MOVED: Mrs. Sarah Adewale
SECONDED: Mr. Emmanuel Chukwu
RESOLUTION: 2021-04-09-01
CARRIED: Unanimously
